blocks.text: Praxis-1 是我们的旗舰世界动作模型，现已在 Apache 2.0 许可下以开放权重向所有人开放。我们于九月发布了 Praxis-1，这是我们的首个世界动作模型，它基于与我们通用世界模型相同的大规模视频预训练构建。我们的发布合作伙伴包括 Noble Machines、Standard Bots 和 Ultra，他们已在各自的硬件上运行该模型：一台足式人形机器人、一台六轴工业机械臂和一台双臂仓储机器人。今天，同一模型向每一位机器人开发者和研究者开放。

blocks.text: 顶尖性能

Praxis-1 是一个 270 亿参数的混合专家扩散 Transformer，能够同时预测视频和动作。它在 NVIDIA 的 RoboLab-120 排行榜上位列世界动作模型之首，并优于所有开放权重的 VLA。在 RoboLab-120 上，Praxis-1 在 1,200 个回合中达到 46.2% 的成功率，相比之下 FLUX 3 Action 为 42.9%，Cosmos3 Nano 为 36.8%，π0.5 为 28.0%。

blocks.text: 适配你的硬件
Praxis-1 从大规模视频中学习物体的行为方式和任务的展开过程，因此在针对任何硬件或领域特定数据进行微调之前，它就已在新形态上具备先发优势。我们的研究表明，作为策略性能的预训练数据，网络视频与遥操作机器人视频效果相当，这意味着一个能力出众的策略，其瓶颈已转变为模型能从多少通用视频中学习。

blocks.text: 与合作伙伴一起，单个 Praxis-1 检查点经过轻度微调即可适配多种形态；借助 LoRA，你无需重新训练完整模型，就能将其适配到自己的形态、相机和任务上。在 Google 的 RT-1 机器人上微调后（该机器人从未出现在其训练数据中），Praxis-1 在 SimplerEnv 上达到 80.0% 的成功率，远高于原始 RT-1 策略的 52.4%。

blocks.text: 为何开放权重

发布 Praxis-1 时，我们承诺会以开放模型的形式交付。美国要在物理 AI 领域保持领先，既需要持续投入硬件和软件，也需要美国模型达到物理应用场景目前尚不具备的互操作性与开放程度。开放权重让硬件开发者能按自己的方式运行、检查和调整世界动作模型。Praxis-1 建立在 Runway 作为 Cosmos Coalition 创始成员所做的工作之上，推动面向物理 AI 的开放世界模型。Runway 与 NVIDIA 正携手开放前沿技术栈，为开发者提供共同的基础，用来解决物理 AI 的种种难题。

blocks.text: Praxis-1, our state-of-the-art world action model, is now available to everyone with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license. We introduced Praxis-1 in September as our first world action model, built on the same large-scale video pretraining behind our general world models. Our launch partners including Noble Machines, Standard Bots and Ultra have been running it on their own hardware: a legged humanoid, a six-axis industrial arm and a dual-arm warehouse robot. Today, the same model is open to every robotics developer and researcher.

State-of-the-Art Performance

Praxis-1 is a 27B-parameter mixture-of-experts diffusion transformer that predicts video and actions together. It is the top-performing world action model on NVIDIA’s RoboLab-120 leaderboard, and it outperforms every open-weight VLA. On RoboLab-120, Praxis-1 reaches 46.2% success across 1,200 episodes, compared with 42.9% for FLUX 3 Action, 36.8% for Cosmos3 Nano and 28.0% for π0.5.

blocks.text: Praxis-1 is available today on GitHub, on Hugging Face with native LeRobot support, and in vLLM-Omni, with hosted inference on Reactor. Everything you need to run and adapt it on your own hardware is released under Apache 2.0, including for commercial use. That covers the weights and the inference and fine-tuning code, with support for both full fine-tuning and LoRA. Praxis-1 runs out of the box across NVIDIA hardware, from data center GPUs like H100 and B200, to workstation GPUs like RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000, to Jetson Thor on the robot itself.

Adapt It to Your Hardware

Praxis-1 learns how objects behave and how tasks unfold from large-scale video, which gives it a head start on a new embodiment before fine-tuning on any hardware or domain-specific data. Our research has shown that web video matches teleoperated robot video as pretraining data for policy performance, which shifts the bottleneck on a capable policy to how much general video a model can learn from.

blocks.text: With our partners, a single Praxis-1 checkpoint has adapted to a variety of embodiments with light fine-tuning, and with LoRA you can adapt it to your own embodiment, cameras and tasks without retraining the full model. Fine-tuned on Google’s RT-1 robot, which never appeared in its training data, Praxis-1 reaches 80.0% success on SimplerEnv, well above the original RT-1 policy at 52.4%.

blocks.text: Why Open Weight

When we announced Praxis-1, we committed to shipping it as an open model. U.S. leadership in physical AI will depend on investment in both hardware and software, and on a level of interoperability and openness from American models that physical use cases don't have yet. Open weights give hardware developers the flexibility to run, inspect and adapt a world action model on their own terms. Praxis-1 builds on Runway’s work as a founding member of the Cosmos Coalition, advancing open world models for physical AI. Together, Runway and NVIDIA are opening frontier technology stacks giving developers shared foundations to build on and solve physical AI challenges.
